name: SUPeR
aliases: Study of Uterine Prolapse Procedures Randomized Trial
question: Does sacrospinous hysteropexy with vaginal mesh lower composite treatment failure compared with vaginal hysterectomy with uterosacral ligament suspension in women with uterovaginal prolapse?

design.blinding: participants and questionnaire assessors masked; surgeons and POP-Q examiners unmasked

arms.label: Sacrospinous hysteropexy with Uphold LITE polypropylene mesh
vaginal hysterectomy with bilateral uterosacral ligament suspension

design.population: Women aged 21 years or older, amenorrheic for at least a year and done with childbearing, who requested vaginal surgery for symptomatic uterovaginal prolapse beyond the hymen (mean age 66).
design.description: Nine-center, participant-masked randomized superiority trial of vaginal prolapse surgery
design.locator: JAMA 2019 Abstract, Methods and Statistical Analysis; Supplement 1 (protocol and SAP); AJOG 2021 Methods and Figure 1

verdictNote: Three-year difference favored mesh but missed significance (P = .06); later reports found fewer failures with mesh.
takeaway: In women with symptomatic uterovaginal prolapse, sacrospinous hysteropexy with Uphold LITE vaginal mesh did not significantly lower 36-month composite treatment failure versus vaginal hysterectomy with uterosacral ligament suspension (24% versus 36%; adjusted hazard ratio 0.61, 95% CI 0.37–1.02; P = .06); mesh exposure was 8%.

reports.label: Trial design and surgical standardization
reports.dateLocator: PubMed entry date 2016-04-08; issue date July-August 2016
reports.citation: Nager CW, Zyczynski H, Rogers RG, et al. The design of a randomized trial of vaginal surgery for uterovaginal prolapse: vaginal hysterectomy with native tissue vault suspension versus mesh hysteropexy suspension (the Study of Uterine Prolapse Procedures Randomized Trial). *Female Pelvic Med Reconstr Surg.* 2016;22(4):182-189.
reports.followUp: Protocol report; planned follow-up 36 to 60 months

delivery.label: Surgeon certification, Uphold LITE
delivery.value: At least 20 sacrospinous ligament dissections, 10 anterior vaginal dissections to the sacrospinous ligament, 10 Capio suture applications, and 5 Uphold LITE procedures performed or proctored.
delivery.note: The site principal investigator reviewed the 5 Uphold LITE cases for complications before sign-off.

delivery.label: Surgeon certification, vaginal hysterectomy with uterosacral suspension
delivery.value: At least 20 vaginal hysterectomies and 20 uterosacral procedures, 5 of the apical procedures in the 12 months before enrollment began.

delivery.label: Mesh hysteropexy technique (Uphold LITE)
delivery.value: Hydrodissection with at least 30 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine with epinephrine or dilute vasopressin; 4 cm transverse anterior incision at least 3 cm from the cervix; extraperitoneal approach to the sacrospinous ligament; mesh delivered 1–2 fingerbreadths medial to the ischial spine; cephalic mesh edge sutured to the cervix; mesh cutting discouraged; apex resuspended without tense arms; 2-0 polyglactin closure; vaginal pack and catheter removed on postoperative day 1.

delivery.label: Uterosacral ligament suspension technique
delivery.value: Performed through the vaginal incision after vaginal hysterectomy; one permanent and one delayed-absorbable 0 or 2-0 monofilament suture per ligament (4 total) extending to the anterior and posterior fibromuscular vaginal wall; no midline plication or culdoplasty.

delivery.label: Concomitant procedures allowed
delivery.value: Native-tissue vaginal wall repairs and anti-incontinence procedures; trachelectomy and cervical shortening were not allowed in the hysteropexy group.
delivery.note: Women expected to have point C at stage 2 or greater after hysteropexy because of cervical elongation were excluded (Table 1).

reports.label: Three-year randomized report
reports.citation: Nager CW, Visco AG, Richter HE, et al. Effect of vaginal mesh hysteropexy vs vaginal hysterectomy with uterosacral ligament suspension on treatment failure in women with uterovaginal prolapse: a randomized clinical trial. *JAMA.* 2019;322(11):1054-1065.
reports.followUp: 36-month primary analysis with failure modeled through 48 months; 169/175 (97%) completed 3-year follow-up (abstract); 153 attended the 36-month visit

results.measure: Model-estimated adjusted 36-month failure incidence; adjusted hazard ratio for interval-censored time to failure through 48 months (retreatment, prolapse beyond the hymen, or bothersome bulge)
results.locator: JAMA 2019 Abstract and Primary Outcome as corrected February 2021 (JAMA 2021;325:696); Statistical Analysis (alpha .047). The supplied PMC6749543 copy predates the erratum and prints 0.62 (95% CI 0.38–1.02) and 26% versus 38%.
results.note: Prespecified significance level for the primary analysis was alpha = .047 (a 2-year interim analysis used alpha = .009), so P = .06 did not meet it. Interval-censored proportional hazards model with a piecewise exponential baseline hazard, adjusted for site and prior prolapse surgery. Proportional hazards were not met (treatment by time P<0.001): the smoothed hazard was higher with hysterectomy except from about 18 to 30 months, so the hazard ratio is an average over follow-up.

results.endpoint: Composite treatment failure, cumulative at the 36-month visit
results.measure: Cumulative (time-to-event, permanent-failure) failure at the 36-month visit, number failed over number assessed; common risk difference in percentage points stratified by site
results.note: First failure type, hysteropexy versus hysterectomy: retreatment 0 versus 1, anatomic and symptom failure 9 (12%) versus 6 (8%), anatomic failure only 12 (15%) versus 22 (28%), symptom failure only 3 (4%) versus 4 (5%). Same measure at 12 months 13/86 versus 21/85 and at 24 months 19/79 versus 28/83.

results.measure: Mean (SD) operative time in minutes; mean difference
results.note: n = 88 versus 87; includes concomitant procedures; unadjusted.

results.measure: PGI-I much or very much better at 36 months; unadjusted risk difference in percentage points
results.note: The planned adjusted model did not converge for this binary outcome.

results.measure: PFDI (range 0 to 300) change from baseline at 36 months, adjusted mean; mean difference
results.note: n = 78 versus 75. Subscale changes: POPDI −40.1 versus −40.2 (P=0.98), UDI −28.3 versus −28.2 (P>0.99), CRADI −11.4 versus −11.6 (P=0.95).

results.measure: Mean (SD) point Ba in cm at 36 months; mean difference
results.note: n = 78 versus 74, unadjusted. Native-tissue anterior repair accompanied 90% of hysteropexies and 71% of hysterectomies, which the authors suggested may account for the small difference. Point C was −5.7 versus −5.8 cm (P=0.74).

results.measure: Mean (SD) POP-Q total vaginal length in cm at 36 months; mean difference
results.note: n = 78 versus 74, unadjusted.

results.measure: PISQ-IR change from baseline among sexually active women at 36 months, adjusted mean; mean difference
results.locator: JAMA 2019 full text (PMC6749543), Table 2; Supplement 2, eTable 3
results.note: n = 23 versus 27. 30/88 (34%) versus 40/87 (46%) were sexually active at baseline; 70 of 175 (40%) overall.

results.measure: Usually or always having pain with intercourse at 36 months, number over number sexually active with the item answered; risk difference in percentage points
results.note: At baseline 10/26 (38%) versus 17/37 (46%).

harms.label: Hysteropexy mesh exposure
harms.locator: JAMA 2019 full text (PMC6749543), Table 2; Results (Adverse Events)
harms.note: Binomial 95% CI 3.3% to 15.7%. Hysteropexy-specific. No mesh exposure, granulation tissue or suture exposure required reoperation.

harms.label: Midurethral sling mesh exposure
harms.note: Women with a concomitant sling only; risk difference −5 percentage points (95% CI −15 to 5; P=0.49).

harms.label: Ureteral kinking recognized and managed intraoperatively
harms.note: Risk difference −7 percentage points (95% CI −15 to −2; P=0.01).

harms.label: Pelvic pain after 12 weeks
harms.note: P=0.40; daily pelvic pain 3/88 versus 4/87.

harms.label: Postoperative dyspareunia, any
harms.note: Risk difference 7 percentage points (95% CI 1 to 14; P=0.03); all treated participants. De novo dyspareunia by PISQ-IR was recorded in 2 hysteropexy and 3 hysterectomy participants.

harms.label: New or worsening stress urinary incontinence
harms.note: Risk difference 7 percentage points (95% CI −4 to 18; P=0.24).

harms.label: New or worsening urgency urinary incontinence
harms.note: Risk difference 8 percentage points (95% CI −4 to 20; P=0.20).

harms.label: New or worsening fecal incontinence
harms.note: Risk difference 8 percentage points (95% CI −1 to 17; P=0.09).

harms.label: Urinary tract infection
harms.note: All treated participants (183), any time during 3 to 4 years of follow-up.

harms.label: Urinary retention
harms.note: All treated participants.

harms.label: Bladder injury
harms.note: All treated participants.

harms.label: Constipation
harms.note: All treated participants.

harms.label: Significant uterine pathology after hysteropexy
harms.note: Stated for the 3 years of follow-up; a cervical polyp was listed in 1/93 (1%) in eTable 4.

delivery.label: Randomized and analyzed
delivery.note: Eight women found ineligible on masked data review were excluded from the primary analysis; 6 of the 175 discontinued at or before 36 months.

delivery.label: Baseline characteristics

values.exp: Age 65.5 (7.3) y; BMI 28.9 (4.0); POP-Q stage 3 in 63 (72%), stage 4 in 10 (11%); symptoms median 26 mo
values.ctl: Age 66.2 (7.4) y; BMI 28.2 (4.4); POP-Q stage 3 in 59 (68%), stage 4 in 9 (10%); symptoms median 33 mo

delivery.note: Stage 2 in 15 (17%) versus 19 (22%). Prior prolapse surgery in 5 (6%) versus 4 (5%); sexually active before surgery 30/88 (34%) versus 40/87 (46%) (Supplement 2, eTable 3).

delivery.label: Surgeons and sites
delivery.value: 34 female pelvic medicine and reconstructive surgery subspecialists at 9 sites.
delivery.note: Surgeon certification required at least 5 recent procedures of each operation (Supplement 2 gives the detailed certification and technique standardization).

delivery.label: Mesh hysteropexy device
delivery.value: Uphold LITE transvaginal mesh support system (Boston Scientific).

delivery.label: Uterosacral suspension
delivery.value: One permanent and one delayed-absorbable suture on each side; no midline plication or culdoplasty.

delivery.label: Concomitant anterior repair
delivery.locator: JAMA 2019 full text (PMC6749543), Table 2; Supplement 2, eTable 1
delivery.note: Risk difference 19 percentage points (95% CI 7 to 30; P=0.002).

delivery.label: Estimated blood loss, mean (SD), mL
delivery.note: Mean difference −6.3 (95% CI −36.4 to 23.7; P=0.68).

delivery.label: Urethral catheter still in at discharge
delivery.note: P=0.96; voiding spontaneously at discharge 52/88 (59%) versus 48/87 (55%).

delivery.label: Days in hospital, mean (SD)
delivery.note: P=0.30; median catheterization days 1 (IQR 1 to 3) in both groups.

delivery.label: Modified Dindo grade IIIb, IIIo or IVa in hospital
delivery.note: Summed from the grade rows (IIIb 1 versus 1, IIIo 3 versus 5, IVa 1 versus 2); P=0.57 for the distribution of grades.

delivery.label: Remained masked to the operation at 36 months
Remained masked overall at 36 months
delivery.note: Among those who stated an assignment, 26 of 30 (87%) were correct.

delivery.label: Randomization
delivery.value: 1:1 in the operating room with an automated web-based system; permuted blocks of 2 or 4 stratified by site.
delivery.note: Participants consented to remain masked to the operation unless a medical indication required unmasking. Study visits were every 6 months.

delivery.label: Sample size
delivery.value: 180 participants planned; power 0.86 to detect a 2-year failure of 8% versus 20% (12 percentage points).
delivery.locator: JAMA 2019 Methods (Sample Size Calculation); Supplement 2, eTable 5
delivery.note: An error in the original calculation (power 0.89 for 10% versus 20%) was found after all participants had completed at least 4 years of follow-up.

delivery.label: Scope of the correction
delivery.value: Errors in the data in the Results section of the September 17, 2019 report were corrected in the Results text, tables and figures; all other information in the Results section was correct and unchanged.
delivery.note: The erratum does not list the changed values.

reports.label: Five-year randomized report
reports.citation: Nager CW, Visco AG, Richter HE, et al. Effect of sacrospinous hysteropexy with graft vs vaginal hysterectomy with uterosacral ligament suspension on treatment failure in women with uterovaginal prolapse: 5-year results of a randomized clinical trial. *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2021;225(2):153.e1-153.e31.
reports.followUp: 60 months; 156/175 (89%) completed 5-year follow-up; median follow-up 60.0 months (IQR 21.0–60.0) with hysteropexy and 45.0 (IQR 9.0–60.0) with hysterectomy
reports.followUpLocator: AJOG 2021 author manuscript, Results and Figure 2 legend

results.measure: Cumulative composite failure at the 5-year visit; adjusted hazard ratio for interval-censored time to failure through 60 months
results.locator: AJOG 2021 author manuscript, Results, Table 2, Figure 2
results.note: A secondary-objective analysis: confidence intervals and P values are descriptive and not adjusted for multiplicity. Proportional hazards were not met (P<0.001), with departure from 18 through 36 months.

results.endpoint: Cumulative composite treatment failure through the 5-year visit
results.measure: Cumulative (permanent-failure) count over number assessed or previously failed at the 5-year visit; site-stratified common risk difference in percentage points
results.note: The risk difference widened from −9 points (95% CI −21 to 2) at 1 year. Most first failures were anatomic or anatomic with symptoms.

results.measure: Any retreatment (pessary or surgery); risk difference in percentage points
results.note: Surgical retreatment 7/87 versus 9/86 (P=0.58); pessary only 1/87 versus 2/86.

results.measure: Met the success definition at every assessed visit through 5 years
results.note: Persistent failure 16.1% versus 22.1%; intermittent success and failure 17.2% versus 26.7%.

results.measure: PGI-I much or very much better at 5 years; risk difference in percentage points
results.note: Reported as 90% versus 96%.

results.measure: Urogenital Distress Inventory change from baseline at 5 years, adjusted mean; mean difference
results.note: The only patient-reported difference between groups; it favored hysterectomy and is not adjusted for multiplicity.

results.measure: Pelvic Floor Distress Inventory change from baseline at 5 years, adjusted mean; mean difference
POP-Q total vaginal length at 5 years in cm, adjusted mean; mean difference
results.note: Point C was −5.8 versus −5.7 cm (P=0.61).

harms.label: Hysteropexy mesh exposure through 5 years
harms.locator: AJOG 2021 author manuscript, Results and Table 2
harms.note: Unchanged from 3 years. Three exposures were found at 6 weeks, 3 at 6 months and 1 at 18 months; all were treated with vaginal estrogen and 1 had office mesh trimming. Two were present at 60 months. None needed operating room management.

harms.label: Granulation tissue after 12 weeks
harms.note: 4 of 12 granulation-tissue cases had office silver nitrate.

harms.label: Suture exposure after 12 weeks
harms.note: Three patients, group not stated, had office suture removal. No suture exposure needed operating room management.

harms.label: Maximum modified Dindo grade III or higher
harms.note: Risk difference −2 percentage points (95% CI −13 to 9; P=0.71). No grade V events.

harms.label: Pelvic pain after 12 weeks
harms.note: Daily pelvic pain 3/90 versus 4/91.

harms.label: New or worsening dyspareunia
harms.note: Risk difference 7 percentage points (95% CI 0 to 15; P=0.10).

harms.label: New or worsening stress urinary incontinence
harms.note: Reported as 21% versus 12%; P=0.11.

harms.label: Midurethral sling mesh exposure
harms.note: Both exposures were asymptomatic.

harms.label: Uterine complications after hysteropexy
harms.locator: AJOG 2021 author manuscript, Table 2 and footnote n
harms.note: Cervical polyp, endometrial polyp, hematometra needing dilation and curettage, and thickened endometrium on imaging with no tissue identified at dilation and curettage or hysteroscopy (1 each).

delivery.label: Completed 5-year follow-up
delivery.note: 156/175 (89%) of the analyzed women.

delivery.label: Remained masked to the operation at the last visit
delivery.note: No group difference; 33/36 who stated their assignment were correct. Unmasking came mainly from insurance paperwork, imaging and conversations with providers outside the study team.

delivery.label: Mesh hysteropexy device
delivery.value: Uphold LITE polypropylene transvaginal mesh (Boston Scientific); bilateral uterosacral suspension used one permanent and one delayed-absorbable suture per side.

reports.label: Risk factors for failure over 5 years
reports.citation: Richter HE, Sridhar A, Nager CW, et al. Characteristics associated with composite surgical failure over 5 years of women in a randomized trial of sacrospinous hysteropexy with graft vs vaginal hysterectomy with uterosacral ligament suspension. *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2023;228(1):63.e1-63.e16.
reports.followUp: 5 years; 173 eligible participants who received the randomized operation
reports.followUpLocator: AJOG 2023 author manuscript, abstract and Methods

results.measure: Adjusted hazard ratio for composite failure per 5 kg/m2 increase in BMI
results.note: Obesity versus normal or underweight 2.9 (95% CI 1.5–5.8); overweight 1.8 (95% CI 0.9–3.5). Planned secondary analysis; significance judged with Bonferroni correction.

results.endpoint: Duration of prolapse symptoms and failure
results.measure: Adjusted hazard ratio for composite failure with symptoms longer than 5 years versus 5 years or less
results.note: Per additional year of symptoms the adjusted hazard ratio was 1.1 (95% CI 1.0–1.1; P<0.005).

results.endpoint: Hysteropexy versus hysterectomy, symptom duration 5 years or less
results.measure: Adjusted hazard ratio for composite failure, hysteropexy versus hysterectomy
results.note: Interaction with symptom duration P=0.07. With symptoms longer than 5 years the hazard ratio was 1.0 (95% CI 0.5–2.1).

reports.label: Ten-year follow-up
reports.citation: Nager CW, Visco AG, Richter HE, et al. Sacrospinous hysteropexy with mesh vs vaginal hysterectomy for treatment of uterovaginal prolapse: 10-year results of a randomized clinical trial. *JAMA Surg.* 2026;161(8):764-774.
reports.followUp: 10 years: 5 years of masked visits every 6 months, then unmasked annual visits in years 6 to 10; 112/175 (64%) entered the extension

results.measure: Composite failure through 10 years, number failed over number analyzed; adjusted hazard ratio for time to failure
results.note: The authors note that the expected additional durability advantage of mesh in years 6 to 10 was not observed.

results.measure: Prolapse, urinary and bowel symptoms, sexual function and dyspareunia
results.note: No group differences were demonstrated, nor in clinically important complications.

delivery.label: Entered the year 6–10 extension
delivery.note: 112/175 analyzed participants (64%).

relations.note: Its uterosacral suspension modified the Shull technique, which the same Pelvic Floor Disorders Network had used in OPTIMAL.
Same comparator, vaginal hysterectomy with uterosacral suspension; SAVE-U tested suture sacrospinous hysteropexy, SUPeR tested mesh hysteropexy.
Same Pelvic Floor Disorders Network and composite failure definition; ASPIRe enrolled women with vault prolapse after hysterectomy.
